Subject: SIG follow-up: SCIM deprovisioning & RBAC defaults

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're progressing through Redwood's SIG and hit a couple of questions on access controls that need more detailed answers for our security review:

1) SCIM deprovisioning: the SIG asks for system behaviour and timelines when a user is disabled in our IdP (we use Okta). Can you confirm the maximum time between a user being deactivated in Okta and their access being fully revoked in Redwood (login, API tokens, and active sessions)? We also need a short description of the deprovisioning flow we can include in our security memo.

2) RBAC defaults: when a customer signs up, what are the default role assignments? Is there an enforced least-privilege baseline, and how are admin roles granted?

3) MFA enforcement: can customers enforce SSO-enforced MFA only, or does Redwood offer an additional account-level MFA option for Console/API access?

We appreciate concrete timelines and any evidence (logs, diagrams) you can attach. Timebox is tight — could we get answers by end of day Wednesday PT?

Best,
Liam
Security Engineer
Acme Health

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. We can definitely get this over to you. High level answers below; Karthik will follow up with the SCIM flow and logs, and Naomi will confirm the RBAC defaults and MFA options. I'm attaching an initial draft of answers (SIG-Access-Answers-v1.xlsx) and a diagram we use internally — you'll see callouts for each enforcement point.

Quick summary:
- SCIM deprovisioning: SCIM user disable events trigger an internal webhook and an asynchronous revocation workflow. API tokens are revoked within the same transaction; web sessions are invalidated on next token refresh (we enforce short-lived session tokens by default). Worst-case propagation to fully revoke an active session is 15 minutes under normal operating conditions; in extreme edge cases (ongoing UDP-based session proxies) it can take up to 30 minutes. We'll provide log samples showing a typical <2 minute path.
- RBAC defaults: accounts start with a single "Owner" role created by the signup flow. The Owner has full admin privileges and can create additional roles. We include a recommended "Least-Privilege" template (Viewer, Operator, Maintainer) that customers can apply.
- MFA enforcement: Redwood integrates with IdP-enforced MFA for SSO. For Console-level access without SSO (rare for enterprise customers), we support optional TOTP-based MFA. We recommend enforcing MFA at the IdP.

We'll send a follow-up with the SCIM event timeline and the exact search queries you can run against our audit logs. Let us know if you want us to redact any details before sharing.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Liam / Acme team — adding detail below and pasting the relevant excerpts from our internal playbook. Quoted previous for context.

On Mon, 2 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800 Marissa Cole wrote:
> Quick summary:
> - SCIM deprovisioning: SCIM user disable events trigger an internal webhook and an asynchronous revocation workflow. API tokens are revoked within the same transaction; web sessions are invalidated on next token refresh (we enforce short-lived session tokens by default). Worst-case propagation to fully revoke an active session is 15 minutes under normal operating conditions; in extreme edge cases (ongoing UDP-based session proxies) it can take up to 30 minutes. We'll provide log samples showing a typical <2 minute path.

Clarifications (concrete):
1) Token revocation: We revoke API tokens transactionally as part of the SCIM disable event. The SCIM handler performs the token revocation API against our token service before returning a 200 to the IdP. That means tokens are not left valid while a separate background job runs. Example log excerpt (sanitized) will show:

- 2026-02-03T13:12:05Z SCIM PATCH user disabled -> token_service.revoke_all(user_id) -> 200 OK

2) Session logout: Web sessions are JWT-based with refresh tokens. When a SCIM disable occurs we mark the user's session state as "revoked" in the session store immediately. Active sessions will be treated as revoked on the next refresh call (typical refresh interval is <= 5 minutes). In cases where the client does not refresh (long-poll connections), the connection may remain usable until the token expiry; default expiry is 15 minutes. So the maximum exposure window in normal config is 15 minutes, but we surface an edge-case maximum of 30 minutes for non-standard network topologies.

3) RBAC defaults: default roles created at account provisioning are:
- role_owner (Owner)
- role_viewer (Viewer)
- role_operator (Operator)
- role_maintainer (Maintainer)
These IDs are present in the attached spreadsheet under the "DefaultRoleIDs" tab. We recommend applying the "role_viewer" and "role_operator" template for least-privilege onboarding.

Evidence we are attaching:
- SIG-Access-Answers-v1.xlsx (filled DefaultRoleIDs tab)
- scim_deprovision_flow.png (sequence diagram)
- audit-sample-20260203.log (sanitized lines pasted below)

Sanitized log lines (examples):
- 2026-02-03T13:12:05Z [SCIM] PATCH /scim/v2/Users/abc123 disabled=true -> revocation started
- 2026-02-03T13:12:05Z [TOKEN] revoke_all(user=abc123) -> 200 OK
- 2026-02-03T13:12:07Z [AUDIT] user=abc123 session_state=revoked

If you want a live demo against a sanitized test account, we can stand one up and run the deprovision flow while you watch — let us know a window.

Thanks,
Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Security (Serving Runtime)
